notes:
User is planning another backyard BBQ with ribs, brisket, pulled pork, burgers, hot dogs, and sides. Preferences include classic/Texas/Kansas City–style BBQ, smoky flavors, and practical guidance. They especially want mac and cheese and are pairing mac and cheese with ribs; ribs have used Sweet Baby Ray’s BBQ sauce, while their current favorite is Kansas City Masterpiece BBQ sauce for ribs and pulled pork. They are open to trying other sauces (suggested Franklin, Bone Suckin’, Stubb’s, or Dinosaur Bar-B-Que) and may serve sauce options so guests can customize pulled-pork sandwiches with coleslaw and pickles.

Brisket plan: low-and-slow smoked brisket, whole 10–12 lb brisket, 225°F smoker, dry rub, and post oak wood chips. They want preparation/smoker setup tips, including trimming excess fat and removing silver skin. Be mindful of food safety and smoker manufacturer instructions.

They also enjoy their new Weber gas grill for quick weeknight dinners and use it for grilled foods. BBQ menu ideas have included burgers and hot dogs with creative toppings/preparations. They want grilled pineapple, like the version Emily brought to their birthday party: use a ripe, firm, sweet pineapple (Hawaiian Gold or Smooth Cayenne), cut into wedges/slices, oil lightly, season, and grill medium-high (375–400°F) until caramelized/lightly charred.

Pulled pork: boneless pork shoulder/Boston butt, seasoned, smoked low and slow, then shredded. Preferred woods include mild apple or cherry, with hickory or pecan as stronger alternatives; avoid overpowering mesquite/oak for pork. Serve pulled pork on a bun with coleslaw and pickles.

Recommended sides: coleslaw, baked beans, grilled vegetables, cornbread, mac and cheese, and potato salad. User especially likes coleslaw to cut the brisket’s richness. A simple creamy-tangy slaw can be made with cabbage, carrots, mayonnaise, apple cider vinegar, Dijon, sugar, salt, pepper, and parsley; chill before serving.
